title: Serving strategy for the text-to-image product
prompt: Your text-to-image product serves a large free tier plus a smaller paid tier on expensive GPUs. Image generation is the dominant cost, and free users vastly outnumber paid ones. How do you allocate model capacity across tiers?
constraint: GPU cost at scale is the binding limit; free users dominate volume, and paid users are the ones who actually need top output quality.

options.why: Directly matches the constraint: the cheap model absorbs the high-volume free traffic that drives GPU cost, while paid users get the quality they pay for. Cost and quality are each spent where they matter most — clear best fit.

Runs the most expensive model on the free tier that dominates volume — exactly where the constraint says GPU cost is the binding limit. Free users bleed margin while gaining quality they didn't pay for.

Simplest to operate and cheaper than fixed-high for free volume, so it respects the cost limit. But it underserves paid users on quality and overspends on free relative to tiering — defensible, not optimal.

Quotas reduce free volume but still pay top GPU cost per free image, leaving per-request cost — the actual driver — unaddressed. It throttles users instead of aligning model cost with willingness to pay.
